_about: The shot encyclopedia: every kind of shot the studio can build, as a recipe the builder can run. Each entry says what the shot is for, how it is built (framing, where people stand, the camera, the motion, the sound), which promises it keeps and which it cannot, and what was measured. `build` is what /build fills in when a person picks the entry; `camera` names a post move the studio performs (never a sentence the engine is asked for).

families.title: Coverage
families.blurb: The shots every scene needs before it needs anything else.

families.title: Camera moves
families.blurb: Done by the studio after the render, so the measured camera equals the requested one.

families.title: People
families.blurb: Framings of one or two people from their packs: whole figures on the plate's ground, faces from the portrait view.

families.title: Place
families.blurb: The place alone, alive: nobody in it, the camera doing the work.

families.title: Dialogue
families.blurb: Lines through the voice packs; the picture holds the speaker.

families.title: Motion beats
families.blurb: In-place actions that pin (turn, crouch, look up); walks stay on LTX.

families.title: Reveals and transitions
families.blurb: Shots whose point is what changes between the first and the last frame.

families.title: Where the camera is
families.blurb: Below eye level, above it, or level with it - performed on the plate by the studio and measured on the take.
